transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kumar (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Product), Marta Ruiz (Constellation), Ethan Cho (Constellation), Samir Patel (Constellation)
---
Auto-generated Summary (brief, may be imperfect):
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture (RA) for joint solution, and next steps for pilot and co-marketing. Discussed VPC/private deployment options, SSO/KMS integration, billing metadata, and benchmark plan. Agreed to draft RA v0 and run an initial benchmark.
---
00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about an hour, um, today we'll focus on the marketplace listing + reference arch for the joint solution, and then cover next steps and security Qs. Marta?
00:12 Marta Ruiz: thanks Jordan, yeah we wanna make sure the listing aligns with our marketplace taxonomy and the RA shows how customers can deploy Redwood in our constellation platform, especially around private VPC and tenancy.
00:27 Priya Kumar: great, quick intro from our side — I'm Priya, SE on the integrations team; Liam's product, he'll cover listing metadata and co-marketing asks.
00:40 Liam O'Connor: hi all, we'll also surface the performance profiles — like the dedicated/reserved model and hosted API differences. Apologies if I mis-say product names sometimes, I might call Redwood Dedicatd or Redwood Private in passing.
00:56 Ethan Cho: big ask from our PMs is we need the RA to include networking (VPC peering, SGs), auth (SSO/SAML support), and key management (KMS/HSM), plus the billing flow for marketplace purchases. Also need clarity on data residency and audit logs.
01:12 Priya Kumar: noted. On the RA we typically include deployment patterns: hosted (API) -> simple integration, dedicated (reserved capacity) -> tenant mapping + VPN/VPC, and private (on-prem/VPC) -> boxed install + KMS. We can sketch network flows and what tunnels/peering are required.
01:30 Samir Patel: for our regulated customers, they prefer the private deployment. Can you clarify what parts of Redwood need outbound internet, or can the control plane be air-gapped?
01:42 Jordan Lee: good question — our private option supports a customer-controlled control plane; the on-prem package can be installed with restricted egress but some telemetry is optional. We'll mark that clearly in the RA.
01:55 Priya Kumar: today let's capture the constraints — e.g., if the control plane is air-gapped, we need a local license server or a throughbrough sync; we can provide a support matrix.
02:10 Ethan Cho: marketplace listing specifics: we need a 1-liner, long description, logos (SVG + PNG), categories, pricing model (usage vs reserved), and any SKU identifiers. Also a security / compliance badge list (SOC2, ISO).
02:27 Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll provide a marketplace bundle file and sample sku names. We usually list both hosted and dedicated SKUs with guidance on when to choose each. We'll also include a sample billing metadata payload for reconciliation.
02:45 Marta Ruiz: on co-marketing, timeline — we want the listing live before our fall partner showcase in mid-Dec. Is that feasible?
02:54 Jordan Lee: feasible if we move quickly — goal: RA v0 this week, security doc follow-up, legal review early next week, then marketplace assets in two weeks. There are internal steps but we can aim for mid-Dec.
03:10 Priya Kumar: technical details — integration points: API key auth for hosted, token-based access for dedicated via our router, and an optional SAML/OIDC path for single sign-on into the console. For KMS: we support both customer-managed keys (via KMS/HSM) or Redwood-managed keys; need to note that on the RA.
03:33 Samir Patel: for networking, typical pattern is VPC peering or private link; do you support AWS PrivateLink or GCP VPC-SC?
03:45 Priya Kumar: we support PrivateLink patterns as reference, and can provide connectors for GCP VPC-SC guidance, but some wording may be vendor-specific.
03:57 Ethan Cho: latency/cost tradeoffs — our infra team wants numbers so they can size instances. Can Redwood share throughput profiles (tokens/sec per instance) and example cost calculations?
04:10 Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll add a performance appendix with median latency and throughput for the curated models — but note those are model-dependent. We'll also provide an example batch sizing guide and quantization options (e.g., int8) which affect cost.
04:29 Jordan Lee: we should also plan a benchmark: Constellation to provide a representative prompt set + target QPS, Redwood runs it on a dedicated pool then returns metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens).
04:45 Marta Ruiz: okay we'll prep a prompt set — Samir, can you own that?
04:50 Samir Patel: yes I'll put together 4-5 scenarios and a sample dataset, aim to deliver by 11/13.
05:00 Priya Kumar: security items — SAML/SSO, RBAC roles, audit logs retention, SOC2/ISO docs, data-in-transit & at-rest encryption, KMS integration, and penetration testing reports. We can share redacted artifacts and our compliance pack.
05:18 Ethan Cho: we have internal questions about multi-tenant isolation for a dedicated pool — how do you guarantee tenant isolation and where does customer data persist?
05:30 Priya Kumar: in dedicated we do tenant mapping at the runtime layer, KV cache is per-tenant, and persistent logs are stored in customer-designated s3 or their storage account when requested. We'll document that in the RA and the security whitepaper.
05:48 Jordan Lee: potential friction: procurement will need Marketplace terms vs Redwood direct contract — we'll add both options to the checklist. Also legal will want SLAs — Redwood Dedicated has SLA options we can include.
06:05 Marta Ruiz: what's the onboarding flow for customers who buy via marketplace but want a private deployment?
06:13 Liam O'Connor: typical flow: marketplace purchase triggers a provisioning ticket, then we run onboarding with infra, schedule a private deploy and validate networking. We'll add that flow to the RA and include sample timelines (2-6 weeks depending on level).
06:30 Samir Patel: can you provide an install script or terraform module for private installs?
06:36 Priya Kumar: yes we'll include a terraform skeleton for the common cloud providers and a checklist for on-prem firewall rules. The install artifacts will be in the RA repo link we share.
06:50 Ethan Cho: auditability — we need to know what audit logs look like (format, retention, and export options).
06:56 Priya Kumar: we emit JSON audit logs with request id, user, model, route, and tokens consumed; retention default is 90 days but can be extended as an add-on. We'll include sample log records.
07:12 Jordan Lee: okay let's talk about the marketplace metadata schema — we need the SKU names, offer descriptions, usage tiers, and sample pricing. We'll send a filled template.
07:25 Marta Ruiz: on co-marketing, we need a joint solution brief and logo guidelines. Also a short case study template. We'll coordinate PR with our comms team.
07:35 Jordan Lee: noted. Any blockers on the security side?
07:39 Samir Patel: just wanting the compliance pack and GDPR/data residency guarantees in writing; also CCPA concerns for some of our customers.
07:48 Priya Kumar: we'll upload a compliance pack (SOC2/ISO3100 - note: transcription may show wrong number sometimes) and a data residency section describing region pinning for both hosted and dedicated.
08:04 Ethan Cho: timeline recap?
08:07 Jordan Lee: action items: Priya drafts RA v0 by 11/16; Jordan sends marketplace checklist + logos by 11/12; Samir provides prompt set and networking constraints by 11/13; Marta confirms co-marketing approver by 11/20. Benchmark scheduled week of 11/23. Follow-up tech sync on 11/16 to review RA v0.
08:28 Marta Ruiz: sounds good, thanks everyone.
08:32 Liam O'Connor: thanks, we'll try to make the RA clear with diagrams and an appendix for security.
08:38 Jordan Lee: thanks all — we'll send notes and links to the RA repo and the marketplace template. Meeting ends.
